NVIDIA reported revenue of $44.1 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended on April 27, 2025 [1]. This represents a 12% increase from the previous quarter and a 69% increase from the prior year [1]. The company incurred a $4.5 billion charge in Q1 fiscal 2026 due to H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, as new U.S. government export licensing requirements diminished demand for H20 products [1]. Prior to these requirements, H20 product sales for the quarter were $4.6 billion, and an additional $2.5 billion in H20 revenue could not be shipped [1].

GAAP gross margin for the quarter was 60.5%, and non-GAAP gross margin was 61.0% [1]. Excluding the $4.5 billion charge, the non-GAAP gross margin would have been 71.3% [1]. GAAP earnings per diluted share were $0.76, and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $0.81 [1]. Without the $4.5 billion charge and its related tax impact, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share would have been $0.96 [1].

NVIDIA's next quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share is scheduled to be paid on July 3, 2025, to shareholders of record as of June 11, 2025 [1].
reference: Nvidia reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $32 billion (up 200% YoY) and net income of $16.8 billion.
